author: deme1744
content:
We have some extra failures from the new malformed-node fixtures added in https://github.com/ethereum/execution-specs/pull/3934. I can make them pass easily by adding structural checks when loading the witness.

But these feel a bit artificial. In real cases the guest can't get to that point. The parent header is bound to the payload's parent_hash, so its state root covers the canonical trie and every node is reached by its hash from there? Or am I missing something?

author: deme1744
content: And it is also not to "catch" such extra faulty nodes in the witness as from what I understand that is removed from the spec and now done lazily?

author: deme1744
content: Also `witness_state_collapse_onto_extension_skips_its_child` is a bit confusing: the stateless input modifier rewrites the parent state and the payload, so the JSON test and statelessInputBytes describe two different chains, basically its two test cases in one fixture. I realized this as I use the test fixtures for both stateless guest run and witness generation comparison, where I also check the witness in the JSON data. The latter would fail. But ok, I can work around this or remove the check all together.
